children: Shares of PG&E and Edison International advanced Tuesday after a report that California lawmakers shelved key wildfire legislation that didn't include liability protection for utilities.
PG&E stock rose 4.9% to $13.93 while Edison International shares gained 7.3% to $57.94. Shares of fellow California utility Sempra advanced 3% to $84.17.

Local California TV channel KCRA's Political Director Ashley Zavala reported at 2:13 p.m. Eastern time that the California State Assembly will "kill" the amended Senate Bill 492. That legislation left out Gov. Gavin Newsom's proposal to limit insurance companies from suing utilities over wildfire-related legal claims.
Zavala cited "multiple" unnamed sources. California lawmakers had been expected to vote on the legislation Tuesday.
Both PG&E and Edison International fell more than 20% on Monday while Sempra declined 3.1% after the bill was amended over the weekend.

The main issue for Wall Street was that the legislation didn't include liability protection for utilities. At a more granular level, firms were concerned there wasn't a long-term funding solution for California's $21 billion wildfire fund, which is paid for by utility shareholders and ratepayers to cover liability.
Wall Street broadly believed California utilities could face liability pressure-and that investors could be left to pay if many claims materialize.
